context.section.permissionsNote: Fields may come from different records. Complete environment records and mixed records remain in their original sections.

context.turn.notFound: No configuration records found for this turn.

demo.case.aborted.guide: Read the recorded interruption message. It does not establish that the invoked command exited.
demo.case.aborted.title: Request interrupted
demo.case.agents-errors.guide: One request hits the agent limit; another targets a missing agent. Neither counts as delivered.
demo.case.agents-errors.title: Agent limit and missing target
demo.case.agents.guide: Review all six operations in order. A wait timeout and an interruption response are separate events.
demo.case.agents.title: Subagents: start, communicate, inspect, wait and interrupt
demo.case.ambiguous-late-command.guide: The same command runs twice in one turn. The late event has no outer call ID, so it stays separate; proximity to the second call is not enough to link it.
demo.case.ambiguous-late-command.title: Repeated command with an ambiguous late event
demo.case.ambiguous.guide: Even when call and response counts match, shared output cannot be assigned to individual operations without evidence.
demo.case.ambiguous.title: Reordered results or a rejected promise
demo.case.cell-image.guide: Jump from a wait to its originating call, then inspect the returned image. Intermediate progress does not replace earlier responses.
demo.case.cell-image.title: Image generation across calls and waits
demo.case.cell-reuse.guide: The first cell 32 has finished. Two later calls both use cell 32, so the final wait has no unique originating call.
demo.case.cell-reuse.title: Reused cell ID
demo.case.cell-stop.guide: Expand wait: the request includes terminate, but the response says Script completed. The request and its outcome are shown separately.
demo.case.cell-stop.title: Termination requested, completion returned
demo.case.cell-terminated.guide: Script terminated confirms that orchestration ended. Earlier output remains on the wait entry.
demo.case.cell-terminated.title: Termination confirmed by the response
demo.case.cell-unresolved.guide: Cell 32 has no final result. A response from a different cell cannot supply its outcome.
demo.case.cell-unresolved.title: Unfinished cell and a wait with no known origin
demo.case.clock.guide: Compare the requested duration with the elapsed duration. All values in this example are synthetic.
demo.case.clock.title: Read the time, complete a wait and interrupt a wait
demo.case.conditional.guide: The orchestration mentions two tools but has only one response. This does not establish that both branches ran.
demo.case.conditional.title: Two tools in conditional branches
demo.case.database-actions.guide: One command records read and listFiles actions. Expand their shared output, then open JSON → Raw log to inspect the database fields.
demo.case.database-actions.title: Database replay: a read and directory listing share output
demo.case.desktop-mcp.guide: Queued means only that opening was requested. The second entry shows workspace dependencies without accessing local files.
demo.case.desktop-mcp.title: Desktop services: queued requests and structured dependencies
demo.case.direct-cua.guide: Both are direct MCP requests. A completion summary and a reset response have different meanings.
demo.case.direct-cua.title: Computer use: completion summary and environment reset
demo.case.direct-patch.guide: The free-form request contains a patch. The native event provides the file changes that can be verified.
demo.case.direct-patch.title: Direct patch request
demo.case.direct-shell.guide: Inspect command startup and continuation without an outer JavaScript wrapper. Replacement characters in the response are preserved; unknown text is not reconstructed.
demo.case.direct-shell.title: Direct terminal calls: start and retrieve
demo.case.directory.guide: The output lists candidate tool names. A name appearing in the catalog is not evidence that the tool was called.
demo.case.directory.title: Look up the tool catalog
demo.case.empty-exit.guide: Exit code 0 is explicitly recorded. Empty stdout is a valid result.
demo.case.empty-exit.title: Successful exit with no output
demo.case.exec-audio.guide: The audio placeholder preserves the response order and media format.
demo.case.exec-audio.title: Orchestration returns text, audio, then text
demo.case.generation-error.guide: Inspect the reference image parameters. If no failure reason was recorded, none is invented.
demo.case.generation-error.title: Reference image edit failed
demo.case.goal-direct.guide: Inspect the budget fields. Marking a goal complete and delivering the work are separate pieces of evidence.
demo.case.goal-direct.title: Direct goal update
demo.case.goal.guide: First inspect the creation conflict caused by an existing goal, then the query snapshot and update response.
demo.case.goal.title: Goals: create, inspect and mark complete
demo.case.invalid-name.guide: The source preserves the historical spelling. TypeError is an orchestration error, not evidence that a patch was applied.
demo.case.invalid-name.title: Calling a tool that does not exist
demo.case.late-command.guide: The exec request and response precede CommandExecution. The UI links them to one call; the raw JSON log preserves all three records in order.
demo.case.late-command.title: Command event arrives after the exec response
demo.case.list-files.guide: File names come from the recorded ls output.
demo.case.list-files.title: List a directory
demo.case.long-read.guide: Inspect the requested line range and expand beyond the first 24 lines. The text and line counts are synthetic.
demo.case.long-read.title: Read a line range and expand more output
demo.case.long-script.guide: The orchestration source stays first. The action is labeled Run command; command source is collapsed by default and can be copied in full. Short output appears once, with extra raw response fields collapsed below.
demo.case.long-script.title: Long command with short output
demo.case.mcp-blocks.guide: Content stays in its original order. The first color chart is valid; the second image is corrupt. Resource URIs appear as text only.
demo.case.mcp-blocks.title: MCP content blocks: images, audio, resources and unknown types
demo.case.mcp-empty.guide: These examples differ only in result shape. A missing response must not be presented as an empty result.
demo.case.mcp-empty.title: Empty arrays, empty responses and missing responses
demo.case.mcp-forbidden.guide: Open the GitHub operation and compare the script status with the service error. No real pull request is created.
demo.case.mcp-forbidden.title: Outer script completed, service returned 403
demo.case.mcp-image.guide: Open the response containing text and an image. A color chart replaces the screenshot.
demo.case.mcp-image.title: External tool returns text and an image
demo.case.mcp-pending.guide: Native MCP call completion and the service's business status are separate states.
demo.case.mcp-pending.title: Call completed, service still pending
demo.case.mcp-protected.guide: Expand the result and JSON. Status and repository name remain readable; credential fields and echoed copies are masked.
demo.case.mcp-protected.title: MCP structured fields: credential masking
demo.case.mcp-status.guide: None of these three states has result content. Each displays the status at the time of its latest record.
demo.case.mcp-status.title: MCP snapshots: running, completed without content, failed without details
demo.case.missing.guide: A missing response does not establish that the call is still running or that it failed.
demo.case.missing.title: Request with no response
demo.case.mixed-terminal.guide: Compare three terminal sessions and a new command. One session cannot be continued.
demo.case.mixed-terminal.title: Poll three terminals and run diagnostics
demo.case.native-agents.guide: Startup and wait events use their own request IDs. Later completion activity is shown separately, keeping a wait snapshot distinct from the subtask's final status.
demo.case.native-agents.title: Agent requests, activity and wait snapshots
demo.case.native-dynamic.guide: Matching tool identities and parameters link a dynamic failure and a later successful command to their own operations. The outer wrapper prints only shared text.
demo.case.native-dynamic.title: Dynamic tool fails while another command returns output
demo.case.native-generation.guide: Expand wait to see the image, revised prompt and save path. A uniquely matching returned image links the native event to the wait call.
demo.case.native-generation.title: Native image generation event returned through wait
demo.case.native-image.guide: The record contains a path but no image block. No substitute image is invented.
demo.case.native-image.title: Native image path without image content
demo.case.native-web-legacy.guide: Open the call to see sources from native WebSearch. An in-page find without a URL shows only its search term.
demo.case.native-web-legacy.title: Legacy web events: sources and in-page find
demo.case.native-web.guide: Open the source title, URL and excerpt. These fields come from the web event.
demo.case.native-web.title: Sources from a native web event
demo.case.orphan.guide: Only a result is recorded. No request is inferred from nearby activity.
demo.case.orphan.title: Tool response with no recorded request
demo.case.output-only.guide: Output text is present, but no exit code was recorded.
demo.case.output-only.title: Script prints only stdout
demo.case.paged-cell.guide: The wait is in the latest eight turns. Follow its origin to load an earlier page, then return to inspect the image.
demo.case.paged-cell.title: Wait and originating call on different pages
demo.case.parallel-image.guide: Expand all four actions. The first three return text; the last returns a color chart. The third command reads two files into one shared output.
demo.case.parallel-image.title: Three reads and an image
demo.case.partial-arguments.guide: Workdir comes from load, while cmd is fixed. The native event precedes the response and links to the original call. Unresolved arguments are labeled; no working directory is invented.
demo.case.partial-arguments.title: Dynamic working directory with a fixed command
demo.case.patch-error.guide: An attempted diff and failure reason are present, but there is no evidence that the file changed.
demo.case.patch-error.title: Patch could not be applied
demo.case.patch.guide: Expand each file's diff. Actual changes come from FileChange, even when the outer response is an empty object.
demo.case.patch.title: One patch: add, modify and move, delete
demo.case.plan.guide: The same step changes from in progress to completed. Each tool entry preserves the plan as it was recorded then.
demo.case.plan.title: Plan before and after an update
demo.case.process-origin.guide: The first command contains unresolved template interpolation. Its startup session_id matches the late event's process_id, linking the event to that call. The second call stays separate, and the startup response remains available.
demo.case.process-origin.title: Process ID links a dynamic command to its result
demo.case.process-reused.guide: Two startup responses record the same session_id. A matching process_id is not enough to choose the more recent call.
demo.case.process-reused.title: Reused process ID with ambiguous ownership
demo.case.questions.guide: Compare choices, answers and accepted. Accepted confirms submission, not that the user selected an answer.
demo.case.questions.title: Answered synchronous question and accepted asynchronous question
demo.case.quiet-poll.guide: The first response has a session ID; the second has exit code 0. Both silent polls retain their raw records.
demo.case.quiet-poll.title: Two polls with no new output
demo.case.script-error.guide: Inspect the syntax error, then open the orchestration source. No terminal exit code was recorded.
demo.case.script-error.title: Orchestration script error
demo.case.script-languages.guide: Multiline Python, JavaScript and shell commands, python3 check.py, and git status all use Run command. Only source presentation differs. The final command shows its recorded nonzero exit code.
demo.case.script-languages.title: Scripts and short commands in different languages
demo.case.search-empty.guide: Compare matching lines, empty output and an error. For rg, exit codes 1 and 2 mean different things.
demo.case.search-empty.title: Search with no matches
demo.case.search-error.guide: Compare matching lines, empty output and an error. For rg, exit codes 1 and 2 mean different things.
demo.case.search-error.title: Search failed: directory does not exist
demo.case.search-hits.guide: Compare matching lines, empty output and an error. For rg, exit codes 1 and 2 mean different things.
demo.case.search-hits.title: Search matches: files and line numbers
demo.case.sequential.guide: The second step uses a directory from the first. Only the packaging result is printed, so its exit code cannot be assigned to the first step.
demo.case.sequential.title: Two sequential commands, only the second result printed
demo.case.shared-read.guide: Open each read operation and confirm that both identify their output as shared.
demo.case.shared-read.title: One command reads several files
demo.case.shell-forms.guide: Compare tail reads, file listings and a pipeline containing an unknown program. Dedicated labels are used only for recognizable command forms.
demo.case.shell-forms.title: Command text only: read, list and an unknown pipeline
demo.case.terminal.guide: Inspect empty input, yes and Ctrl-C for session 17. The exit code appears only in the final response.
demo.case.terminal.title: Terminal session: poll, input and interrupt
demo.case.unicode-command.guide: Unicode escapes are decoded according to string rules and matched character by character to the late command. The recorded source is never executed.
demo.case.unicode-command.title: Command with Unicode escapes
demo.case.unknown.guide: Two scripts without fixed tool names. Only explicitly recorded output establishes what happened.
demo.case.unknown.title: Dynamic tool names and pure computation
demo.case.unlinked-command.guide: The earlier call runs a different command. The standalone event keeps its output and explains that no matching call was found; its event type is not used as a tool name.
demo.case.unlinked-command.title: Execution event with no matching call
demo.case.view-error.guide: Keep the path and recorded error. Do not display a substitute image.
demo.case.view-error.title: Unreadable image path
demo.case.wait-interrupted.guide: Inspect the wait response to distinguish interrupting a wait from terminating the background cell.
demo.case.wait-interrupted.title: User interrupts this wait
demo.case.web-media.guide: Search results retain their sources. PDF requests retain page numbers; synthetic color charts stand in for page images.
demo.case.web-media.title: Web image search and PDF screenshots
demo.case.web.guide: Combined queries use example domains. Results that cannot be assigned to individual operations remain shared.
demo.case.web.title: Web: search, open, find and click
